"Independent mathematical research for SoringP1 #301 and GitHub issue #48, read-only: do not edit repository or post externally. Investigate whether there exists a sound, polynomial-time checkable adversary invariant that forces a comparison obstruction from the initial n-element antichain under EVERY sorting strategy, not merely from an arbitrary reachable partial order. This is distinct from the entropy-deficit identity audit and the Sergeev finite-bound investigation already completed. Read docs/research-structural-lower-bounds.md, docs/research-hardness-boundaries.md, docs/research-one-ply-obstruction.md, and docs/research-obstruction-next.md. Check GitHub issue #48 comments for any prior result. Falsifiable deliverable: either (a) a concrete candidate invariant with a proof sketch that it forces an obstruction from the antichain for all n, with a clear polynomial-time verification procedure, or (b) a precise proof that any such invariant must fail, with an explicit counterstrategy construction, or (c) documentation that this is already resolved or blocked with evidence. Distinguish between: (i) a bad reachable poset that is hard to sort, and (ii) a poset an adversary can force against every height-k root strategy. Do not conflate these. Include independent-check pointers. No claim of final SORT-BOUND-U resolution."
